elements.text: Known cancer patient
Manage and refer urgently:
If abdominal aortic aneurysm likely: avoid giving IV fluids even if BP < 90/60 (raising blood pressure may worsen rupture).
If BP < 90/60 or pancreatitis likely, give sodium chloride 0.9% 500mL IV over 30 minutes, repeat until systolic BP > 90. Continue 1L 6 hourly. Stop if breathing worsens.
If complicated pyelonephritis likely: first collect urine for MCS and then give ceftriaxone 1g IV2/IM.

If kidney stone likely: give sodium chloride 0.9% 1L IV 6 hourly. If pain severe, give morphine 5-10mg IM or diluted morphine 3-5mg IV. If giving IV, dilute 10mg morphine with 9mL of sodium chloride 0.9%. If needed, give another 1mL/min until pain improved, up to 10mL. Repeat morphine after 4 hours if needed. Stop if BP < 90/60. Discuss/refer.
If patient known to have cancer, refer same day.
BACK PAIN

1Sepsis is any of: SBP < 80, pulse ≥ 100, respiratory rate > 30, confusion. 2Do not mix Ringer's lactate and IV ceftriaxone. 3Avoid if peptic ulcer, asthma, hypertension, heart failure, kidney disease, pregnant. If patient also taking aspirin, advise to wait at least 30 minutes after taking aspirin before taking ibuprofen.

Approach to patient with back pain not needing urgent attention • If flank pain with leucocytes/nitrites on urine dipstick, uncomplicated pyelonephritis likely: send urine for microscopy, culture, sensitivity. Give ciprofloxacin 500mg 12 hourly for 7 days and paracetamol 500mg-1g 4-6 hourly (up to 4g in 24 hours) as needed for up to 5 days. If no better after 2 days, refer. • If unexplained rash or lesion/s of skin/genitals/anus/rectum/mouth/eyes and ≥ 1 of: headache/backache/body pain, swollen lymph nodes, temperature > 38.5°C, fatigue, sore throat/nasal congestion/ cough, consider mpox 40. • Does patient have any of: cough, weight loss, night sweats or fever?

Unsure No Mechanical back pain likely • If BMI ≥ 25 156. • If low mood, stress or anxiety 98. • Reassure patient that back pain is very common, and usually gets better on its own. Explain that pain does not always mean a disease or cancer, and tests cannot always show the reason for the pain and often are not needed. • Advise patient to be as active as possible, continue normal activity and avoid resting in bed. • Advise patient that regular exercise may prevent recurrence of back pain. • Give pain relief: paracetamol 500mg-1g 4-6 hourly (up to 4g in 24 hours) as needed for up to 5 days. - If poor response after 1 week, add ibuprofen3 400mg 8 hourly with/after food for up to 5 days. - If still poor response add tramadol 50-100mg 6 hourly (max 400mg/24 hours) for up to 5 days. • If pain persists > 2 weeks, or unable to cope with daily activities/work, refer for physiotherapy. • If pain persists ≥ 3 months, assess 76, and refer to doctor. If bladder/bowel disturbance or numbness/ weakness develops, refer urgently.
